about: LedgerMath runs small benchmarks on real AWS machines several times a day and keeps every execution as a Run. A Series is the Runs of one benchmark, parameter set, build, instance type and Availability Zone ID; a versioned Method turns its Runs into a Derivation. This is version 1 of the data API: static JSON files cut from the Derivations and the daily price files, each kind with a JSON schema.
versioning: Version 1 only ever gains fields. A field, once in a v1 file, keeps its name, its type and its meaning, and a reader ignores any field it does not know: that is why no object in a v1 schema forbids members it does not list. A new Method, or a new version of one, is a new key beside the old ones. A change that would break a reader is published as v2, beside v1.
figures: Every number is exactly as the Methods' Derivations hold it: nothing is rounded, and nothing is computed that the Derivations do not hold, apart from counts of a Series' Runs and the start times of its oldest and newest Run, taken from its points. A duration is in nanoseconds of the Run's clock unless its field's name says otherwise; a moment is a UTC time, to the nanosecond, as the Run records it.

evidence.about: The evidence is served at the keys of LedgerMath's bucket of Runs, under the same address as the API: each point of a Series file links its Run file (evidence) and its boot's summary (boot_summary). A Run file names its binary, streams and dumps by hash, sha256:<hex>; each is a blob at blob_url_template with {hex} replaced by the 64 hex digits.

recent_rounds.about: Added by hand to this test fixture, in the shape the API is to give: the three rounds of boots that ended with the newest Run, counted from the boot records of 2026-11-19.
